messages:
sasha: Customer Finly reports a sudden billing spike and 5xxs starting ~08:10 UTC. They say they have region pinned to eu-west-1 but traces show a lot of traffic served from us-west-2. ticket# 4589

maya: can you paste a sample trace id and a curl repro? also any account-level routing overrides?

sasha: trace ids: r-trace-33a7, r-trace-33a8. Quick repro I ran from our EU test node: 
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" -H \"x-redwood-region: eu-west-1\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Response: 503 Service Unavailable + body: "overflow: routed to fallback region".

jordan: pulled proxy logs for the request windows. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-12T08:10:11Z] route=eu-west-1 queue_len=128 policy=AUTO_SPILLOVER -> action=spillover target=us-west-2 reason=capacity_exhausted
[2026-03-12T08:10:12Z] route=eu-west-1 -> backend=us-west-2 latency=240ms status=200
[2026-03-12T08:10:13Z] client=finly service=streams retry=1
```
Looks like the eu-west pool hit queueing threshold and auto-spilled to us-west-2.

lee: billing note: cross-region egress and extra token compute on us-west adds extra cost; if a tenant is pinned but still autospills, they will be billed for the destination capacity. That explains the spike.

maya: metrics show queue_length (eu-west-1) > 120 for sustained 3m around 08:09-08:14. Our admission controller threshold is 100. Autoscaler did not spin up extra nodes fast enough because the scale-policy for eu-west is conservative for this customer. Query: 
```
# prometheus quick
sum(rate(redwood_serving_queue_length{region=\"eu-west-1\"}[1m])) by (queue) = 125
```

sasha: customer reported retries from their side too. They saw 503 then retried immediately which amplified load.

jordan: root cause chain: traffic spike -> queue exceeds admission threshold -> AUTO_SPILLOVER triggers -> requests hit us-west -> increased latency for those requests -> client retries -> more load on eu-west on backfill and on us-west inbound -> observed billing bump. Also noticed some requests got 401 when routed due to token audience mismatch when cross-region routing hits different auth shard.

support-bot: flagged tenant finly for manual routing override.

maya: short-term mitigation options:
- disable AUTO_SPILLOVER for tenant finly (quick, prevents cross-region egress but may increase 429s)
- increase eu-west admission threshold + bump reserved capacity for 15m
- add short client-side 100-200ms jitter/backoff guidance to reduce immediate retry storms

lee: recommend disabling spillover for this tenant while we investigate billing recalc. I'll prepare a credit estimate.

jordan: to disable spillover for tenant finly: 
```
rictl tenants patch finly --set routing.policy.spillover.enabled=false
```
I'll run that now (will be quick).

jordan: executed the override at 08:20 UTC. Confirmed via config: routing.policy.spillover.enabled=false for tenant=finly.

ops-bot: action created: INC-8922 "Investigate spillover scaling mismatch for eu-west" assigned to eng-runtime.

maya: follow-up items:
1) eng-runtime: investigate why autoscaler didn't add capacity (logs show scale decision delayed by 45s)
2) infra: validate auth shard replication to avoid 401s on spillover
3) customer success: communicate temporary disable + expected 429 behaviour and billing credit plan

sasha: Customer notified about temporary change and expected behavior. They accepted the temporary 429 risk.

lee: starting billing impact calc — initial estimate shows ~3x compute cost for the spilled requests window (08:09-08:22). Will post final by EOD.

maya: moving to eng-runtime channel to loop in Jordan and Priya on autoscaling policy tweaks.

support-bot: thread closed for now; will reopen on new observations.
